sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Rep. Max Miller Seeks Reelection Amid Custody Case
cards.content: Rep. Max Miller is running for re-election in Ohio's 7th Congressional District, a seat once considered safe for Republicans, but now a key battleground due to controversies surrounding Miller's personal life. Miller's high-profile custody case, which includes allegations of abuse from his ex-wife, is scheduled to go to trial just days after the election. The race has seen millions spent by both parties, with Republicans investing over $9 million and Democrats spending $17 million. Despite the controversies, Miller remains defiant, saying he is confident his constituents know him and will win the race. His opponent, Democrat Brian Poindexter, claims to have momentum on the ground, but the race has been marked by dueling ads highlighting the pasts of both candidates.

cards.title: Germany protests turn violent, with rioting and arrests reported
cards.content: Germany saw widespread protests and violence on Saturday, with rioters looting shops and clashing with police in cities like Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne, and Hamburg. The peaceful protests, organized by Gen Z regelt, aimed to address issues like underfunding in schools, high living costs, and public spending cuts. However, as night fell, the demonstrations turned violent, with reports of smashed windows, molotov cocktails, and arrests. Authorities reported around 18,000 protesters, with many incidents of violence and vandalism, including the smashing of a gun shop window. German officials have criticized the violent turn of events, comparing it to similar unrest in France, where over 320,000 people protested on the same day.

cards.title: Starmer Calls for European Defence Framework Amid US Shift
cards.content: Sir Keir Starmer, the former UK prime minister, has emphasized the need for a common security framework in Europe, stating that the shift in the US's defence relationship with Europe is permanent rather than a temporary phenomenon. He warned that the US will no longer 'bankroll' European allies, and that Europe must take on more responsibility for its own defence and security. Starmer also emphasized the importance of pan-European co-operation and co-ordination on defence and security, noting that the EU is changing to respond to these new circumstances. He cautioned that Europe's periphery is core to its defence, and that the EU cannot be the only one responding to this challenge. Starmer's remarks were made at a British Irish Chamber of Commerce dinner in Dublin, where he also received an honorary life membership.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Comet theory on life's origin may be flawed, simulations suggest
cards.content: The popular theory that comets brought life-starting molecules to Earth, allowing life to emerge, may not be accurate, according to new computer simulations. The research found that comets, when they impact the Earth, would likely destroy the fragile organic molecules, making it unlikely for life to have begun on our planet through comet delivery. The study's lead author, Richard Anslow, suggests that instead, life may have emerged through alternative means, such as Earth's primordial soup or asteroids, which could have delivered the necessary building blocks of life. The research also raises the possibility that ancient Mars, with its lower impact velocities, could have been more suitable for HCN delivery, adding a new dimension to the question of whether Mars once supported life.

cards.title: Proteins linked to Alzheimer's, Parkinson's aid human reproduction
cards.content: Researchers at Columbia University have discovered a new role for proteins associated with Alzheimer's and Parkinson's disease in human reproduction. Amyloid fibrils, tiny protein fibers found in semen, can transport RNA into sperm cells, helping to move genetic material into sperm. This discovery could lead to new methods for delivering gene therapies and has implications for RNA delivery in medicine. The study found that amyloid fibrils can carry large RNA molecules that can produce functional proteins in developing embryos. The researchers also demonstrated that these protein fibers can enter sperm cells and deliver RNA, which could have significant implications for understanding the role of RNA in embryonic development and gene regulation.

cards.title: Uranus and Neptune Have Different Origins, Study Finds
cards.content: A new study suggests that Uranus and Neptune, long considered planetary twins, actually have different origins and chemical histories. While they share similarities, Neptune's deep atmosphere contains more oxygen than Uranus', indicating that they formed from different regions of the protoplanetary disk. This discovery challenges the long-standing belief that the two ice giants developed from the same reservoir of cosmic ingredients. The study uses atmospheric observations and computer models to investigate the planets' chemical compositions roughly 4.5 billion years ago, when they formed. The researchers propose that Neptune may have accumulated building blocks that originated closer to the young Sun and subsequently migrated outward, giving it a different chemical history from Uranus. This finding has implications for understanding how planets form and evolve throughout the galaxy, and could shed light on the formation of similar-sized planets around other stars. The study was published in the September 2026 issue of Astronomy & Astrophysics and was co-authored by scientists from Southwest Research Institute.

sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Quercetin slows lung cancer cell division in lab tests
cards.content: Researchers at the University of Erlangen-Nürnberg found that quercetin, a compound found in citrus fruits, onions, and buckwheat, slowed lung cancer cell division and movement in laboratory experiments. At the highest dose tested, cell migration nearly stopped. The study, published in Cell Death Discovery, also showed that quercetin affected several processes involved in cancer growth, including the reduction of two proteins that can help tumors evade the immune system. In addition, the compound increased levels of interferon-alpha-2, a signaling molecule that helps the immune system defend against tumors. The researchers believe that a quercetin-rich diet could support treatment for lung cancer and may even have preventive effects. However, more studies are needed to confirm the findings and establish whether the effects seen in cells and mice extend to humans.

cards.title: Stenting, Surgery No Boost to Cognitive Skills, Study Finds
cards.content: A recent study led by Randolph Marshall at Columbia University found that opening severely narrowed carotid arteries, also known as stenting or surgery, does not improve cognitive skills compared to medication alone. The study, known as CREST-H, enrolled 291 patients with carotid artery narrowing and found that cognitive scores improved slightly in both groups, but patients who underwent a procedure did no better than those treated with medication alone. This challenges the idea that reopening these arteries can reverse cognitive decline in patients without associated symptoms. The study's findings have already changed practice, with more patients receiving stents, but the results suggest that patients should not expect the procedure to improve their thinking skills beyond what medication alone provides.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: Odisha boosts rescue efforts after Cyclone Arnab floods seven districts
cards.content: The Odisha government has increased rescue and relief efforts in seven districts severely affected by heavy rainfall caused by Cyclone Arnab on October 28. The rain, possibly influenced by a second cyclonic system, caused rivers to swell, triggering floods and landslides that destroyed roads and bridges, leaving villages isolated. The districts of Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, and Rayagada were most affected, with roads and bridges washed away, leaving many marooned.

cards.title: Antarctica Turns Green and Red Due to Penguin Droppings Fueling Algae
cards.content: Antarctica, known for its vast expanses of white ice and snow-covered mountains, is unexpectedly turning green and red in some areas. This phenomenon has caught the attention of scientists who are trying to understand the connection to climate change. One factor contributing to the colorful patches is penguin droppings, which provide nutrients to microscopic algae growing on the snow. The scientists suspect that this natural process may accelerate local melting, adding to the effects of a warming climate. The impact of penguin droppings on the melting of Antarctica's snow is still being studied, and the effects are not yet fully understood.

cards.title: Srinagar's Water Crisis Worsens due to Climate Change
cards.content: In Srinagar, a water crisis has been ongoing for years, causing daily struggles for residents like Mehak and Zamrood. The absence of a regular water supply has led to the installation of tanks and a hand pump at their homes. Climate change is affecting Doodh Ganga, a vital source of drinking water, causing erratic water supply, low flow, and dry taps. The river's water availability is decreasing due to rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and declining snowmelt. The Kashmir Valley's 24 watersheds, including Doodh Ganga, are experiencing similar impacts.

cards.title: Bristol's Full Cycle Shapes Early Jungle and Drum and Bass Sound
cards.content: Bristol's underground music scene has been a driving force in the evolution of jungle and drum and bass music, with the city's Full Cycle collective being a key player in shaping the genre's early sound. In the early 1990s, the collective, which included DJ Krust, DJ Die, producer Roni Size, and DJ Suv, drew inspiration from Jamaican sound systems, acid house, and hip hop, creating a new and innovative sound. This experimental sound, characterized by its fast tempo, syncopated rhythms, breakbeats, and reggae samples, resonated with the city's youth, and the collective's music quickly gained popularity through underground parties and radio shows. The group's breakthrough came with the release of their album 'New Forms' in 1997, which included the hit track 'Brown Paper Bag,' and their subsequent win of the Mercury Prize, making them the first drum and bass group to receive the award. Today, jungle and drum and bass music continue to thrive, with artists from Bristol and beyond pushing the boundaries of the genre.

cards.title: Traitors contestant lands lead roles and business success after reality TV appearance
cards.content: Former The Traitors contestant Kieran Tompsett, 46, from Stevenage, Hertfordshire, has transformed his life after appearing on the show in 2022. He decided to attend Ashley Walters' Kingdom Drama School, training for a year and a half and landing roles in three or four films, including Masters of the Universe. Tompsett was initially overwhelmed by the loss of privacy that came with being in the public eye, but he has since secured a lead role in a horror film and runs an AI workflow automation company. He will also appear in the dark comedy Damaged Goods. Prior to The Traitors, Tompsett worked as a solutions consultant.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: White House Tries to Bridge Economic Data Gap with Voters' Perceptions
cards.content: The White House is facing a familiar dilemma, where economic numbers aren't necessarily bad, but the public mood is. The issue is the disconnect between the solid economic data, such as low unemployment and strong growth, and the high prices that voters are paying at supermarkets and gas stations. President Donald Trump has promised to bring prices down, but the latest inflation report confirms that prices remain high. Trump's administration has tried to shift the focus from prices to economic indicators like GDP and the stock market, but voters are judging the economy by what they pay at the supermarket and whether they can keep up with bills. The challenge for Trump is to bridge the gap between the economic data and the public's perception of the economy. His predecessor, Joe Biden, faced a similar challenge during the 2024 election campaign, but ultimately failed to convince voters that the economy was working for them.

cards.title: Naomi Nomi Revolutionizes Fashion with Quality, Long-Lasting Clothing
cards.content: Naomi Mishkin, the founder of Naomi Nomi, is revolutionizing the fashion industry by producing high-quality, long-lasting clothing at a higher price point. The average customer starts with one shirt and returns for three more within six months, as they realize the value of her products. Mishkin's approach is a departure from the fast fashion industry, which has mastered the art of cutting production costs to the bone. She uses cotton and wool, making her shirts pricier than fast fashion, but lasting longer. Naomi Nomi's success is attributed to the growing backlash against companies that prioritize profit over quality and the environment. The fashion industry has undergone significant changes over the past few decades, with a shift towards planned obsolescence and the use of cheaper materials. However, some consumers are now looking for brands that offer quality, durability, and sustainability, and Naomi Nomi is capitalizing on this trend.

cards.title: Nscale to Build UK's Largest AI Data Centre in Loughton, Despite Microsoft Pullout
cards.content: Nscale, a tech company, has reaffirmed its plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre in Loughton, Essex, despite Microsoft's decision to pull out of the project. Microsoft had agreed to fund a supercomputer at the site, but its involvement has been terminated. Nscale is exploring alternative power sources and maintaining a strong relationship with Microsoft for other projects globally. The data centre was expected to receive its power supply by the end of this year, but this has been delayed until the 2030s due to a London-wide grid issue. The project is expected to create 250 permanent jobs when it opens.
